Article: No constitutional provision. Text: The Australian Constitution (1901) contains no explicit provision on future generations, intergenerational equity, or environmental rights. Country: Australia (AU) Jurisdiction type: national Region: Oceania Section: dedicated_legislation Ambition tier: leader Ambition score: 81 Relevant signal count: 13 Item 1. Name: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (EPBC Act) — Intergenerational Equity Principle. Year: 1999. Scope: national. Status: active. Summary: Australia's primary national environmental law. Section 3A explicitly enshrines intergenerational equity as one of the core principles of ecologically sustainable development: 'the present generation should ensure that the health, diversity and productivity of the environment is maintained or enhanced for the benefit of future generations.' This is one of the strongest statutory intergenerational equity provisions in Australian law, though it applies primarily to environmental decision-making.. Source: https://www.dcceew.gov.au/environment/epbc Item 2. Name: Climate Change Act 2022. Year: 2022. Scope: national. Status: active. Summary: Australia's first standalone climate change legislation, passed under the Albanese government. Enshrines a 43% emissions reduction target by 2030 and net-zero by 2050 into law. Requires the Climate Change Authority to provide annual progress reports. While not framed as a future generations law, its long-term statutory targets inherently protect future generations by locking in a decarbonisation trajectory.. Source: https://www.dcceew.gov.au/climate-change/policy/australian-government-climate-change-policy Item 3. Name: Wellbeing of Future Generations Bill 2025. Year: 2025. Scope: national. Status: proposed (before Parliament as of 2025). Summary: Private member's bill introduced by Dr Sophie Scamps MP (independent). Directly inspired by Wales' Well-being of Future Generations Act. Proposes a Federal Wellbeing Framework, a duty for government and public bodies to consider long-term intergenerational wellbeing, a Future Generations Commissioner, and a National Conversation on future generations. Active civil society campaign led by Foundations for Tomorrow and the Intergenerational Fairness Coalition.. Source: https://www.sophiescamps.com.au/future_generations_bill_2025

Country: Australia (AU) Jurisdiction type: national Region: Oceania Section: judicial_precedents Ambition tier: leader Ambition score: 81 Relevant signal count: 13 Item 1. Case: Sharma v Minister for the Environment [2021] FCA 560; [2022] FCAFC 35. Year: 2021. Court: Federal Court of Australia (trial); Full Federal Court (appeal). Relevance: Eight Australian children sued the federal Environment Minister, arguing she owed them a common law duty of care not to approve a coalmine extension that would contribute to climate harm. At trial (2021), Justice Bromberg found the Minister had a novel duty of care to protect children from climate harm — the first such finding globally, referencing the government's 'responsibility for the interests of future generations in the health of the environment.' On appeal (2022), the Full Federal Court unanimously overturned this, holding no such duty existed. Despite the reversal, the case catalysed global climate litigation and established that Australian courts would engage with intergenerational climate arguments.. Outcome: Duty of care found at trial (2021); unanimously overturned on appeal (2022). No duty of care owed by the Minister.. Source: https://envlaw.com.au/sharma/
